families.EMA cross: Fast EMA crossing a slow one. The oldest trend rule there is; included as a floor -- anything that cannot beat this is not worth its complexity.
families.SuperTrend flip: Enter on the bar SuperTrend changes direction. Pure trend following; lives or dies on how choppy the tape is.
families.MACD cross gated by ADX: Only take MACD crosses while ADX says a trend is actually present. The gate is the whole idea -- MACD alone fires constantly in chop.
families.Donchian breakout: The turtle rule: buy the N-bar high, sell the N-bar low. Included because it is the honest baseline for every breakout idea that dresses itself up.
families.PSAR flip with EMA filter: Parabolic SAR flips, but only in the direction of a slow EMA. SAR alone whipsaws; the filter is what makes it testable.
families.Ichimoku cloud break: Tenkan crossing Kijun while price is on the right side of the cloud. Spans are NOT displaced forward here -- displacing them is look-ahead and it is why this looks magical on charts.
families.Aroon cross: Aroon up crossing down measures how RECENTLY the extremes were made, which is a different question from how far price moved.
families.TRIX zero cross: A triple-smoothed rate of change crossing zero. Very slow and very quiet -- the opposite failure mode to the fast families.
families.Hull MA slope: Hull turns faster than an EMA for the same period. Trading its slope is the cleanest test of whether that speed is signal.
families.Bollinger fade: Close outside the band, then close back inside. Waiting for the re-entry is what separates this from catching a knife.
families.RSI extreme with trend filter: Buy oversold only above a slow EMA, sell overbought only below it. Fading against the trend is the most reliable way to lose slowly.
families.VWAP z-score reversion: Fade a stretch of N session sigmas from VWAP. The single most cited intraday reversion rule, and the one most often tested without a session reset -- which turns VWAP into a slow moving average and the result into fiction.
families.VWAP trend: The opposite bet to the one above, on the same line: hold in the direction of VWAP rather than fading it. Running both settles which one the tape actually pays.
families.Keltner fade: Same shape as the Bollinger fade but on an ATR channel, so it does not widen just because the last twenty closes disagreed.
families.Williams %R reversal: A pure range-position oscillator with no smoothing, so it reacts a bar or two before RSI does. Whether that is early or just noisier is exactly what the test is for.
families.CCI extreme: CCI leaving +/-100 after an excursion. Its mean-absolute deviation denominator makes it behave differently from RSI on the same bars, which is the only reason to test both.
families.Stochastic cross in the extreme: %K crossing %D, but only while both are already stretched. The crossover on its own fires several times an hour.
families.MFI extreme: RSI weighted by volume. Included specifically to test whether volume adds anything to the oversold read or just lags it.
families.Bollinger fade with volume confirmation: The band touch, but only when volume spiked -- the published claim is that the spike is what separates a reversal from a band-walk. This measures the claim.
families.FVG retest: Price returns into an unfilled fair value gap and closes back out of it in the gap's direction. The core ICT entry, with every threshold made explicit so it can actually be measured.
families.Order block retest: The last opposing candle before an imbalance, traded when price comes back to it. Distinct from the gap itself: the block is a candle body, the gap is the space it left.
families.Break of structure continuation: Trade the BOS in the direction of the established structure. Judged on the close, never the wick -- an intrabar poke that closes back inside is the move this is meant to exclude.
families.Change of character reversal: The first structural break AGAINST the prevailing trend. The same indicator as the family above, taking the opposite event -- so the pair answers whether structure pays for continuation or for reversal.
families.Liquidity sweep reversal: Price takes out an equal high or low -- resting stops -- and closes back inside. The textbook stop-hunt entry.
families.Premium/discount with structure: Only buy in the lower half of the trailing range and only sell in the upper half, with structure agreeing. A location filter rather than a signal in its own right.
families.Squeeze release: Bollinger bands compressed inside the Keltner channel, then released. Direction comes from the squeeze momentum, which is the part everyone leaves out and then wonders why it is 50/50.
families.ATR expansion breakout: A bar whose range is a multiple of recent ATR, traded in its direction. Crude, but it is the cleanest available proxy for 'something just happened'.
families.RSI divergence: Price makes a lower low while RSI makes a higher one. Reported only when the second pivot is CONFIRMED, which is several bars late -- divergence read on the pivot bar itself is the most common look-ahead in published strategies.
families.Opening range breakout: The first N minutes set the range; trade the first close outside it. The range is only usable AFTER it completes -- using it while forming is what makes every ORB backtest look brilliant.
families.Opening range fade: The mirror bet: the first push out of the opening range is the one that fails. Run against the family above so the tape decides rather than the fashion.
families.EMA pullback in trend: Trend by the slow EMA, entry when price touches the fast one and closes back with the trend. Buying a dip inside an uptrend rather than buying a dip.
families.Three-bar momentum: Three closes in the same direction with expanding range. The simplest possible momentum definition, present as a control: if an elaborate family cannot beat this, the elaboration is not doing anything.
families.CONTROL: random entry: A coin flip on a fixed schedule, using the identical stop, target and cost model as every real family. This is the null hypothesis with a seat at the table. If a strategy's score sits inside the spread of these, it has found noise.
families.CONTROL: always long: Buy on a fixed schedule and manage it with the same stop and target as everything else. Not quite buy-and-hold, but it is the drift benchmark: a long-biased strategy on a rising tape has to beat this before any of its cleverness counts.
